name: SceneSearch
subtitle: Multimodal video retrieval with reproducible evaluation.
short_description: An AI-engineering project that searches a video library using natural language and returns timestamped moments supported by transcript and visual evidence.
workload_note: A working envelope of roughly 10 to 12 hours a week, adjustable. This is a plan, not a commitment, and it is not necessarily time on top of existing study. See the curriculum mapping below.
links_note: No repository or demo exists yet. Links appear here when there is something real to point at.

overview.problem: Editors, creators and researchers need to find a specific moment in a video library without watching everything. Transcript search alone misses what is shown rather than said, and browsing by eye does not scale past a few hours of footage.
overview.solution: Index a small video collection along two independent tracks, the spoken transcript and sampled frames, then retrieve across both and return a playable, timestamped moment with the evidence that supports it.
overview.scope: Owned or appropriately licensed video, one language, a collection starting at roughly two to five hours. Audio extraction and timestamped transcription, timestamped frame sampling, keyword and semantic transcript retrieval, image-text embedding retrieval over frames, combined retrieval, and playable results with supporting transcript excerpts or frames.
overview.status_note: Planned. Nothing is built. Every measurement on this page reads "not yet measured" because no experiment has run.

example_queries: Find the moment where the presenter demonstrates the dashboard, rather than just mentioning it.
Find a nighttime crowd scene with no visible presenter.

research_question.question: When does combining visual evidence with transcript retrieval improve video search, and what are the quality, latency and cost trade-offs?
to_investigate: Whether adding visual retrieval improves recall over transcript retrieval alone, and on which query types.
What frame-sampling density is enough before extra frames stop paying for themselves.
What combining the two tracks costs in query latency and indexing time.
How the system should behave when nothing in the library actually answers the query.
already_established: Nothing yet. No result on this page has been measured.
research_question.caveat: A text-only reranker reads the transcript, not the picture. It cannot confirm that something appears on screen, and this project will not claim that it can.

architecture.note: Proposed design, not a built system. No screenshot on this page is a real interface.

stages.name: Video ingestion
stages.detail: Owned or licensed source files, with provenance and permissions recorded per video.

stages.name: Transcription and frame sampling
stages.detail: Audio extracted and transcribed with timestamps; frames sampled at a chosen density, each keeping its timecode.

stages.name: Text and visual embeddings
stages.detail: Transcript segments embedded for semantic search; frames embedded in a shared image-text space.

stages.name: Persistent indexes and metadata
stages.detail: Vector indexes plus a metadata store holding timecodes, source video and provenance.

stages.name: Candidate retrieval and optional reranking
stages.detail: Retrieve candidates from each track, combine them, and rerank only where a baseline shows it is justified.

stages.name: Timestamped playback with evidence
stages.detail: A result plays at its timecode and shows the transcript excerpt or frame that produced it.

cross_cutting.name: Evaluation
cross_cutting.detail: A fixed query set and scoring harness that any configuration can be run against.

cross_cutting.name: Profiling
cross_cutting.detail: Latency, indexing time, memory and storage measured per configuration rather than estimated.

baselines.name: Keyword transcript retrieval
baselines.note: The floor. If a later system cannot beat this, it is not earning its complexity.

baselines.name: Semantic transcript retrieval
baselines.note: Catches paraphrase the keyword baseline misses.

baselines.name: Visual retrieval
baselines.note: Frames only, no transcript. The test for queries about what is shown.

baselines.name: Combined transcript and visual retrieval
baselines.note: The configuration the research question is actually about.

baselines.name: Optional reranking
baselines.note: Added only if a baseline comparison shows a gap worth closing.

experiments: Frame-sampling density against retrieval quality and indexing cost.
Smaller against larger embedding models, if feasible.
CPU and GPU placement, chosen in response to a measured bottleneck rather than in advance.

measures.name: Ranking quality (nDCG where labels support it)
Temporal overlap with labelled relevant intervals
Indexing time and cost per hour of video

design: Begin with 50 to 75 manually reviewed queries, expanding toward roughly 100 to 150 if that proves feasible.
Cover spoken-content, visual-only, mixed-evidence, near-match and no-answer queries.
Separate development and held-out videos where feasible, and do not tune against held-out results.
Report uncertainty and failure modes rather than a single headline number.
Do not rely on model-generated ground truth alone; every query in the set is reviewed by hand.

deliverables: Evaluation scripts, and results once they exist
responsible: Owned or appropriately licensed content only.
Provenance and permissions recorded per source video.
No employer data, code or proprietary workflow.
Model and dataset licences checked before use.
Unsupported claims and retrieval failures written down rather than omitted.
out_of_scope: Kubernetes or comparable infrastructure the project does not need
Fine-tuning before a baseline shows the need

budget.excludes: Existing hardware, personal time and course subscriptions.
budget.caveat: A planning envelope, not a vendor quote. Actual cost depends on compute, storage and how far the experiments run. No provider pricing is quoted on this page.

hiring_relevance.disclaimer: This is a portfolio objective, not a hiring outcome. Building it guarantees nothing, no organisation is involved in or endorses it, and nothing here describes any employer's current openings.

Implement keyword and semantic transcript search
roadmap.exit: A user can search a small video collection and play a relevant returned segment.

build: Map results back to source-video intervals
roadmap.exit: Transcript-only and visual-only baselines can be compared, with documented failure examples.

build: Expand reviewed queries toward 100 to 150 if feasible
Measure quality, latency and indexing cost
roadmap.exit: A reproducible experiment table showing where combining modalities helps and where it does not.

build: One or two measured optimisation experiments
Proposed usability testing with three to five external participants
roadmap.exit: An external user can use the system, and at least one engineering trade-off is measured and written down. Major features freeze at the end of the month.

Prepare a concise and a detailed explanation

skill_audit.note: Each SceneSearch skill checked against the courses and phases already recorded on this site, before considering anything new.

rows.reasoning: Deep-learning fundamentals are covered twice over. What is not established from the recorded titles is PyTorch specifically: tensor handling, batching for inference, and moving models between CPU and GPU. The from-scratch phase is deliberately framework-free, which is useful for understanding and does not by itself teach the framework.

existing: CSCA 5422 Modern AI Models for Vision and Multimodal Understanding
rows.reasoning: Already in the plan in both curricula. One CU course names multimodal understanding directly, and a from-scratch phase is dedicated to it. No addition is warranted on coverage grounds.

existing: CSCA 5454 Advanced Data Structures, RSA and Quantum Algorithms
Graph Search, Shortest Paths, and Data Structures
rows.reasoning: Classical data structures and graph search are covered. Approximate nearest-neighbour search over vectors, and combining two ranked lists into one, are not. This is the clearest genuine gap, and it is narrow enough to close with a documentation reference and the project itself rather than a course.

Evaluation design is the strongest thing on this site: two shipped artifacts turn on held-out evaluation, pre-registration and baselines allowed to win. What is missing is the information-retrieval vocabulary specifically, Recall@k and nDCG, which is a small amount of reading on top of practice that already exists.

One from-scratch phase touches the audio side, which is where transcription lives. Video decoding, frame sampling and keeping timecodes aligned across tracks appear nowhere. This is engineering work rather than course material, and the project is the natural place to learn it.

existing: MLOps Tools: MLflow and Hugging Face (Duke)
CSCA 5028 Applications of Software Architecture for Big Data
rows.reasoning: Already selected in the AdTech pathway, including a course that names MLflow directly. Adding another deployment course would duplicate a commitment already made.

sequencing.finding: No course anywhere on this site carries a start date, a completion date or an hours estimate, and every one of the 53 records reads Planned. Only the from-scratch pathway is marked in progress, and all twenty of its phases are themselves Planned.
consequences: I cannot say whether any foundation is scheduled before or after SceneSearch needs it, because nothing is scheduled at all. Every sequencing question is undetermined rather than satisfied.
I cannot say whether 10 to 12 hours a week is additional time or shared time, because existing weekly study time is not recorded anywhere. No claim is made here that the combined plan is feasible.

The foundations SceneSearch leans on hardest, deep learning, computer vision and multimodal understanding, are all Planned with no date. That is the dependency to resolve before November, by scheduling them, by narrowing the project, or by accepting that the project teaches them.

proposed_changes.note: Nothing below has been added to the curriculum. These are proposals that need your decision, kept separate from the established plan.

items.title: Add a PyTorch fundamentals course for November
items.case: The one candidate with a real argument. November's build needs a reproducible embedding pipeline in the first month, and the recorded deep-learning coverage does not establish framework-specific skill.
items.against: It is an addition to a curriculum that already holds 53 planned courses, none of them started. Applying an existing deep-learning course would be preferable if its syllabus covers PyTorch, which the recorded titles do not settle.
items.recommendation: Hold until either the candidate syllabus or the existing deep-learning syllabus is checked. Adding a course should be the last resort, not the first.

items.title: Close the retrieval gap with documentation, not a course
items.case: The Sentence Transformers retrieve-and-rerank guide covers candidate retrieval and reranking directly, at the scale the gap actually is. It is a reference to read, not a credential to collect.
items.against: None. This is the cheapest option that closes the gap.
items.recommendation: Adopt. Reference material, scheduled for January, no change to the course plan.

items.title: Learn video processing by doing it
items.case: Decoding video, sampling frames and keeping timecodes aligned is engineering practice. It is learned faster by building the ingestion stage than by taking a course about it.
items.recommendation: Adopt. The project absorbs this gap.

items.title: Treat the multimodal and advanced-deployment candidates as unnecessary for now
items.case: Multimodal retrieval is covered by a CU course and a from-scratch phase already selected. Deployment and profiling are covered by two Duke courses already selected, one of which names MLflow. Adding more would duplicate existing commitments.
items.against: If a syllabus check later shows the existing courses miss something specific, this can be revisited.

items.title: Schedule the foundations, or narrow the project
items.case: The curriculum has no dates. SceneSearch has five dated months. Those two cannot both be true without a decision: either the deep-learning and multimodal material gets dates before it is needed, or SceneSearch narrows so it depends on less of it.
items.recommendation: Your call. If the two conflict, the brief says reduce SceneSearch scope first and protect the foundations, evaluation and reproducibility.
